points: HPV is a double-stranded DNA virus. Common cutaneous types are **1, 2, 3, 4, 10, 27, 29 and 57**.
It infects **basal keratinocytes**, producing hyperkeratosis and new virus particles.
Spread is by skin-to-skin contact, fomites (swimming pools, changing rooms), and **autoinoculation**. A line of warts along a scratch is the pseudo-Koebner phenomenon.
Incubation takes weeks to months. The wart burden is higher with dermatitis or **immunosuppression** (transplant, HIV).

items.name: Common (verruca vulgaris)
items.t: Rough hyperkeratotic papules; black or red dots are thrombosed capillaries

items.name: Plantar
items.t: Inward-growing and painful (myrmecia), or clustered ‘mosaic’ warts; **interrupt the skin lines**

items.name: Plane (plana)
items.t: Flat-topped, skin-coloured, often numerous; spread by shaving

items.name: Filiform / digitate
items.t: Thin fronds on a narrow base

items.name: Periungual / subungual
items.t: Around or under the nail; risk of nail dystrophy

cards.name: Corn / callus
cards.clue: At a pressure site; skin lines continue through it; no capillary dots

cards.name: SCC / keratoacanthoma
cards.clue: Rapid growth, ulceration or tenderness, often in an older or immunosuppressed patient. **Refer**

items.t: Rapid growth, bleeding, ulceration or an atypical appearance: consider **SCC** and refer.
**Immunosuppressed** patient (transplant, HIV) with extensive or recalcitrant warts: refer to dermatology.
Extensive facial or periungual warts where destructive treatment risks scarring or nail damage.
Diabetes, peripheral neuropathy or vascular disease: avoid self-treatment with salicylic acid or cryotherapy on the feet.

pearls.t: No treatment ‘kills’ HPV instantly. Treatment removes virus-bearing skin, and recurrence is common until immunity clears that type.
Duct-tape occlusion has mixed evidence. It is an optional add-on, not a cure.
Periungual warts: avoid aggressive destruction near the **nail matrix**.
Advise flip-flops in communal showers, not sharing towels, and covering verrucae for swimming.
